title: North-eastern District
description: The Hamlet's most ruined quarter, where its streets meet the sea. Buildings list precariously on the eroding cliffs, while the shore path winds treacherously toward the cove. This district bore the brunt of horrors emerging from the manor, its once-proud institutions now standing as hollow shells.
summary: The most ruined quarter where the hamlet meets the sea, with buildings on cliffs and a treacherous shore path.

title: Shore Path
description: A precarious trail carved into the rocky coastline beneath the Estate's towering cliffs. Beginning as simple stone steps near the hamlet, it grows increasingly narrow as it winds beneath the manor's looming presence, eventually becoming little more than a ledge above the churning waters. Those who dare to follow it to its end speak of an enormous cavern mouth where the cove's dark waters vanish beneath the earth.
summary: A precarious trail carved into the rocky coastline, winding beneath the manor towards a cavern mouth.

title: Covert Jetty
description: A sheltered dock extending from a narrow stair cut into the cliff face, designed for discrete deliveries to the manor above. The Ancestor's ingenious pulley system still spans the height of the cliff - chains and hooks dangling like forgotten gallows against the rock face. The greedy crew that made his final delivery disappeared beneath these unnaturally dark waters, their anchor dragging them to unknown depths.
summary: A sheltered dock with a pulley system, designed for discrete deliveries to the manor from the sea.

title: Condemned Shack
description: A shattered wooden shanty clinging to a rocky islet along the shore path, linked to the mainland by a cracked stone footbridge. Built atop the stump of an ancient lighthouse, its roof and upper floor have completely caved in, leaving only a rotted, wind-whipped shell where seawater pools over cracked floorboards.
restored: A sturdy timber shelter anchored securely upon the ancient lighthouse foundations. Fresh-cut cedar shingles, reinforced walls, and a small lookout turret keep the coastal gales at bay, providing dry, elevated quarters with a commanding view of both the cove's cavernous mouth and the manor's cliffside hoist.
summary: An isolated dwelling constructed upon ancient lighthouse foundations on an offshore islet, providing cliffside lodging.

title: Smuggler's Hideout
description: A flooded chamber beneath the condemned shack, its entrance half-submerged in the dark waters. This concealed berth once sheltered small boats from prying eyes, cleverly built into the old lighthouse's base. Iron rings for mooring still protrude from the algae-covered walls, though none have dared tie up here since the waters turned black.
summary: A hidden, flooded chamber beneath the condemned shack, built into an old lighthouse base for concealing small boats.

title: Athenaeum
description: Once the Estate's premier center of esoteric learning, now a gutted shell of shattered windows and toppled, sodden bookshelves on the coastal bluff. A tattered banner still clings to its facade—its faded motto 'Scientia Est Lux Lucis' ('Knowledge Is Light') reading more like a grim warning. The domed rooftop observatory lies caved in, its brass telescopes long since smashed or carried off by fleeing scholars.
restored: A sharp-gabled academic hall of dark timber and slate, crowned by a working copper-domed observatory overlooking the sea. High arched windows illuminate long reading tables, secure display cabinets of eldritch relics, and shelves of salvaged occult texts. Above the entrance flies a pristine banner bearing the institution's renewed vow: 'Scientia Est Scutum' ('Knowledge Is A Shield').
summary: An esoteric academy and domed observatory dedicated to occult research, artifact cataloging, and containment studies.

title: Geological Study Hall
description: A sheared stone tower on the coastal bluff whose seaward wall has collapsed into the abyss. The final survey expedition's equipment lies exactly as they left it—drilling rigs hanging over open air, core samples laid out beside rain-soaked logbooks open to their final entries. None of the scholars ever returned from the depths they were measuring.
restored: A tall observation tower of reinforced masonry and timber buttresses, anchored deep into the cliff bedrock. While modern scholars use its rooftop spire and instruments to track the crystalline corruption spreading from the Miller's comet, the old magnetic needles remain inexplicably drawn to something buried deep beneath the manor's foundations.
summary: A cliffside research tower equipped with seismographs and surveying instruments for studying the Estate's bedrock and cosmic mineral anomalies.

title: Sewer Entrance
description: Heavy iron bars seal this ancient tunnel mouth, installed hastily when the Ancestor's early experiments with rat hybridization proved too successful. The bars show signs of persistent gnawing, while distant squeaks and scratches suggest the ratfolk still thrive in their underground domain. A faded warning sign hangs askew: 'Sealed by order of the Estate.'
summary: A heavily barred ancient tunnel mouth, leading to underground domains of thriving ratfolk.

title: Raven's Row
description: A well-maintained street of distinguished townhouses, its northern end marked by ruins where the district's scholarly institutions once stood. While those buildings closer to the manor were the first to fall to its horrors, the southern stretch remains a testament to the hamlet's former prosperity. An ornate metal arch spans the street's entrance, the Estate's Noble Raven worked into its weathered ironwork.
summary: A well-maintained street of distinguished townhouses, a testament to the hamlet's former prosperity, leading to scholarly ruins.

title: Old Bakery
description: A sturdy three-story building marking the start of Raven's Row, its ground floor still bearing the worn baker's sign. Though the shop itself lies dormant, the massive stone ovens remain intact, and on quiet mornings, old residents swear they can still catch the ghost of fresh bread on the wind. The upper floors offer comfortable lodging, with large windows overlooking the morning bustle of the market square.
summary: A sturdy three-story building at Raven's Row, once a bakery with intact ovens, now offering comfortable lodging.

title: Merchant's Row House
description: The grandest of Raven's Row's surviving townhouses, built to display its original owner's prosperity. Three stories of faded elegance rise above a small courtyard, its distinctive bay windows offering views down to the harbor. Though time has dulled its decorative flourishes, the spacious rooms and practical storage spaces remain appealing to those of mercantile inclination.
summary: The grandest townhouse on Raven's Row, built to display prosperity, with spacious rooms and harbor views.

title: Cryptographer's Residence
description: A peculiar narrow house whose previous owner's paranoia proved surprisingly practical. Multiple locks secure every door, hidden compartments riddle the walls, and curious mechanical features suggest secrets yet undiscovered. Despite its oddities - or perhaps because of them - the house remains surprisingly well-preserved.
summary: A peculiar narrow house with multiple locks and hidden compartments, suggesting undiscovered secrets.

title: Professor's Villa
description: The last grand house before the ruins begin. Its northern wing lies collapsed where the horrors first struck, but the surviving rooms retain their dignified character - wood-paneled studies and book-lined walls speaking to quieter days. The original occupant, like many of the district's prestigious inhabitants, now rests beneath a wooden cross on the abbey's northern slope.
summary: A grand house on Raven's Row, with dignified wood-paneled studies and book-lined walls, a symbol of scholarly life.

title: Schoolhouse
description: Set apart from the main street in its own small courtyard, the hamlet's schoolhouse endures despite all odds. The Caretaker maintains a semblance of education here between his other duties, his rambling lectures occasionally straying from arithmetic to apocalyptic prophecy. Despite the stains on the ceiling and the occasional inexplicable scratching from within the walls, the neat rows of desks and determinedly organized shelves of primers suggest an institution refusing to succumb to the surrounding chaos.
summary: The hamlet's enduring schoolhouse, where education is maintained with neat rows of desks and organized primers, despite the surrounding chaos.

title: Manor Staircase
description: The foot of a long, winding stone staircase ascending directly from the northeast district to the manor far above. While nobility would arrive through the Courtyard path by the Dower House, this more practical path served the manor's staff and, later, the endless stream of workers and miners hired for the Ancestor's excavations. Iron lantern brackets still line the way, though their lights no longer guide workers home in the evening dark.
summary: A long, winding stone staircase ascending from the district to the manor above, primarily used by staff and workers.

title: Aqueduct
description: Crumbling stone arches march through the district's ruins before driving directly into the bedrock of the manor's hill. Once carrying fresh water to the hamlet, the channel is now stained with a foul, rust-colored sludge. A massive wooden portcullis, reinforced with heavy iron bands, blocks the cavernous tunnel entrance where the structure breaches the hillside. Standing near the rotting timbers, one can feel a hot, fetid draft and hear the echoing, guttural squeals of the things that now claim the tunnels beyond.
summary: A ruined stone watercourse entering the manor's hill, blocked by a heavy wooden portcullis that barely muffles the squealing horrors within.

title: Amphitheater
description: A ruined open-air theater carved into the cliff edge, facing the churning sea. The crowning gallery has collapsed into massive piles of rubble that choke the tiered seating below, while salt frost and weeds have split the stage into tilted slabs slick with spray. Whatever was once performed here, no playbill survives to tell.
restored: A grand semicircular stone theater carved into the coastal bluff. Orderly tiers of grey stone seating descend toward a flagged stage overlooking the water, crowned by a gothic arched gallery that shelters spectators from coastal winds. The venue once more hosts guild ceremonies, traveling players, and the Town Crier's dramatic soliloquies.
summary: A tiered cliffside stone amphitheater with a covered gothic gallery, designed for assemblies and performances overlooking the sea.

title: Archaeological Base Camp
description: A leaning, three-story staging house at the foot of the manor approach, its lower porch buried in debris and slide-rock. Smashed amphorae, broken pickaxes, and muddy excavation crates spill from the rotting awning, abandoned when the things unearthed in the oldest ancestral foundations turned upon the diggers.
restored: A robust, three-story timber lodge serving as the primary field station for subterranean excavations. Barrels of iron-headed shovels and mattocks flank the stone threshold, while the covered porch is packed with cataloged pottery jars, antique mirrors, and architectural fragments recovered from the ancient castle strata beneath the manor.
summary: A three-story excavation headquarters and staging post in the northeast district, outfitted for delving into the ancient ancestral ruins beneath the manor.
